collections.title: Seva & dignity
collections.description: The work of our hands, the meals we share, and the dignity we owe one another.

collections.title: Courage & conscience
collections.description: Stories of asking difficult questions and living by what matters.

collections.title: Lives transformed
collections.description: An encounter, a question, a new direction. Stories of a life opening to change.

stories.title: The Bread at Lalo’s Table
stories.subtitle: A meal, a feast, and the work behind them.
stories.description: Guru Nanak accepts a carpenter’s hospitality. A powerful man demands to know why his own feast was refused.

stories.title: The Shade of a Shared Table
stories.subtitle: Mata Khivi and the kitchen at Khadur
stories.description: A remembered bowl of rice opens a window onto Mata Khivi’s place in the life of the early Sikh community.

stories.title: A Thread That Would Not Break
stories.subtitle: Young Nanak asks what a sacred thread can hold.
stories.description: At a ceremony arranged by his family, Nanak questions whether a mark worn on the body can transform the life within it.

stories.title: The Water He Carried
stories.subtitle: Amar Das on the road to Khadur
stories.description: Before he became the third Guru, Amar Das walked the road of service. One stormy night, that road brought him to a weaver’s door.

stories.title: The House That Hid Its Darkness
stories.subtitle: Sajjan’s welcome concealed a terrible cost.
stories.description: A host offers shelter to travellers. Guru Nanak answers with a hymn that asks what lies beneath a spotless surface.

stories.title: Water Turned West
stories.subtitle: A familiar gesture, interrupted by a question.
stories.description: At Haridwar, Guru Nanak throws water in the opposite direction from the gathered pilgrims, and an argument becomes a searching conversation.

stories.title: A Needle for the Next World
stories.subtitle: Duni Chand could keep a fortune. Could he keep this?
stories.description: A wealthy host accepts a small object from Guru Nanak, then discovers that the simple promise attached to it cannot be kept.

stories.title: The Milk and the Gold
stories.subtitle: A gift offered before daylight brings an unexpected discovery.
stories.description: A villager brings milk to Guru Nanak and Shaikh Brahm. The traditional account asks what can be received, and what can be missed.
